main_concern: --ignore-user-config is a broad suppression flag that may suppress more user-level config than the targeted interactive brainstorming skill. Without a carrier probe or actual E2E run, there is no evidence the flag does not also interfere with project-level or role-level configurations needed for correct E2E operation. The self-check passed with --skip-carrier-probe, which directly contradicts the acceptance contract's new requirement for independent carrier-probe verification of project-level hooks and session behavior.
minimum_fix: Before running Round 20: (1) execute a carrier probe with --ignore-user-config enabled to verify project-level hooks still fire, (2) log which specific user-level configs are being suppressed vs preserved, and (3) do not skip the carrier probe in the Round 20 self-check. If the carrier probe reveals any suppressed config that E2E roles depend on, narrow the suppression to target only interactive/approval-gating skills rather than all user config.
missing_evidence: Actual E2E run logs showing Loom roles complete without stalling on interactive prompts
Carrier probe results verifying project-level hooks still function when --ignore-user-config is active
Inventory of what specific user-level configs exist and which are suppressed vs preserved by the flag
reality_delta: The patch adds a config isolation mechanism (CODEX_ROLE_IGNORE_USER_CONFIG flag, build_codex_role_argv, receipt fields) and updates the acceptance contract to require independent verification. However, the mechanism has not been proven end-to-end: the self-check that passed skipped the carrier probe, the flag is broader than the targeted fix, and no behavioral evidence (actual E2E run) exists yet. The code-level reality changed; the behavioral reality has not been demonstrated.
top_risks: --ignore-user-config may suppress project-level hooks or role-level configs that E2E roles actually need, causing silent failures or incorrect behavior in Round 20
The self-check --skip-carrier-probe pattern creates a verification debt loop: each round patches the previous round's issues while deferring the hardest verification to the next round

Role prompt text instructions against human-approval flows are a soft guard; if --ignore-user-config fails to load or is inadvertently disabled, the original interactive stall can recur with no hard fallback
